outcome.description: You transfer the credits. The pirate grunts acknowledgment and peels away. Cheaper than repairs, you tell yourself.
You power up weapons and angle your shields. The pirate grins . They were hoping you'd say that.
The enforcer accepts payment without ceremony. They mark your transponder as 'cleared' . Whatever that means out here.
You hold course and charge weapons. The enforcer's professional demeanor cracks . They expected compliance, not resistance.
You transmit a confident-sounding string of authorization codes. The enforcer hesitates, then backs off . They can't risk tangling with someone who might have real backing.
The AI ship accelerates to attack speed. Its hull shimmers with adaptive plating.
You cut comms and burn hard. The AI vessel does not pursue. Its final transmission: "NOTED. NEXT TIME."
The Corsair King opens with a broadside that rocks your ship to its bolts. This is the fight of your life.
You punch the engines and break away. The King does not pursue. You were beneath notice.
The Iron Maw opens its jaws. The heat hits your shields before the weapons do.
You cut engines and drift backward. The Iron Maw does not follow. It has other prey.
The Phantom flickers. For one moment it is solid, and in that moment it fires.
You kill active sensors and drift away on momentum. The Phantom flickers once more and vanishes.
The Leviathan turns toward you. Your ship feels very, very small.
You blind-jump to anywhere that is not here. Your hull groans as the gravity well pulls, but you break free. Barely.
The Collector deploys weapons you have never seen before. This is what happens when one ship has everything.
You boost away, tractor beams clawing at your hull. You escape. This time.

You transfer the credits. The autopilot responds: 'Thank you for your payment! A receipt has been transmitted to your comms. Please note: robbery satisfaction surveys are available at the following frequency. We value your feedback! Have a great day!' The ship cheerfully peels away to find its next victim. You stare at the receipt. It has a customer loyalty stamp. Four more robberies and you get one free.

You open fire. The autopilot responds with evasive maneuvers and return fire, all while broadcasting: 'We're sorry you've chosen the inconvenient option! Please hold while we process your objection!' The weapons are old but the autopilot's reflexes are machine-fast.

You hail the ship and ask it to rob itself. There's a long silence. Then: 'Processing... processing... ERROR: cannot rob self. Robbery requires distinct victim entity. But if I am both robber and victim... does the transaction net zero? Is all robbery ultimately self-defeating?' The weapons power down. The ship drifts away, its running lights blinking in what you choose to interpret as deep thought. You've weaponized philosophy.

You transfer the credits. Vex is surprisingly professional . They escort you through two debris fields and past a cluster of ships that definitely would have tried something. At the beacon, Vex peels off with a wave. "Pleasure doing business. Tell your friends." Extortion with a smile. The Crimson Reach way.

You tell Vex where they can put their offer. There's a long pause, then a chuckle. "Brave. Stupid, but brave. Your call, Captain." Vex breaks off and vanishes into the debris field. You spend the next thirty minutes with your weapons hot and your nerves frayed, but nothing happens. This time.

You negotiate Vex down to a flat guide fee in exchange for safe corridor mapping data. Vex seems amused . And a little impressed. They hand over a surprisingly detailed nav chart of the local debris fields. "You've got hustle, Captain. I respect that." The chart alone is worth more than the fee.
